note: Adapted from Krishna 1961, A generic revision and phylogenetic study of the family Kalotermitidae (Bulletin of the American Museum of Natural History 122: 307—408), the original in English; the alate is recorded in the original as Unknown. The description is placed under the entry for the characters of the new genus Tauritermes, but the accompanying Fig. 56 is labelled as the soldier of T. taurocephalus (Silvestri) (paratype, Corumba, Mato Grosso, Brazil), and is in fact the soldier description of this species.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: (Fig. 56) Head phragmotic; the anterior part dark and sculptured; frontal outline steep; frons with 2 well-developed processes separated by a wide concavity; no horn-like processes above or below the antennal fossae; antennal carinae slightly raised and rounded; a very faint ridge between the frons and the vertex, not sharp as in the genus Procryptotermes. Compound eyes distinct, unpigmented. Antennae 10—11-segmented; segment 3 wider and longer than segment 2. Mandibles slender and long, with a prominent basal swelling. Pronotum as wide as the head; anterior margin raised and covering the back of the head, deeply concave, wavy and denticulate. Femora not swollen. Tibial spur formula 3:3:3.

sections.label: Nymph
sections.text: Mandibles as in the genus Cryptotermes: in the left mandible the first plus second marginal teeth are smaller than the third marginal tooth (Fig. 57); in the right mandible the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth is distinctly longer than the molar plate (Fig. 57). The media of the forewing bud is weak and unsclerotised, running between the radial sector and the cubitus as far as the wing apex.
